newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end down as stocks erase losses.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end down as stocks erase losses.

text.p: *Japanese government bond futures end slightly higher after giving up earlier gains following Nikkei's rebound from earlier lows.
*Activity led by dealers though some buying by investors seen at the long-end.
"People were just watching stocks. Activity was largely led by dealers," said a brokerage house trader.
A weak stock market is seen as supportive for JGBs as it underscores the market's view that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will maintain its low interest rates policy.

The March rose to an intraday high of 126.01 in the morning but ran out of steam after Bank of Japan (BOJ) vice governor Toshihiko Fukui said long-term interest rates were moving in low ranges, traders said.
His remarks were relayed to reporters by Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Minister Taro Aso.
Traders said players became a bit more cautious after some politicians and key government officials expressed concerns about a weak stock market in the morning.

Taku Yamazaki, chairman of the policy-making committee of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, was quoted by Jiji news agency on Tuesday as urging the government to consider measures to tackle the problem of weak stock prices. Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday that the Ministry of Finance (MOF) will continue to watch movements in the stock market with deep interest.
Although the day's activity was led by dealers, some buying of cash JGBs by investors was detected at the long-end of the yield curve, traders said.
Traders said JGBs were likely to continue testing higher levels as the demand-supply condition remained favourable.
"Profit-taking selling of JGBs ahead of the fiscal year-end is expected to continue, but its impact may be offset by a strong demand for cash JGBs," said a trader at another brokerage house.
"The March is likely to climb above 126.00 when the market reopens on Thursday," said the first trader.
Tokyo's financial markets will be closed on Wednesday for a national holiday.
Market sources said MOF was likely to hold an auction of six-year JGBs on Friday.
The amount of the offer was likely to be around 500 billion yen and the coupon was likely to be set at around 1.6 or 1.7 percent, traders said.
"After last week's strong 10-year JGB auction, the six-year JGB auction is likely to see a good result," said a trader at a long-term credit bank's securities unit.
